title: How to Handle a Bad Day at the Office
script: Narrator: [warmly] Everyone has bad days at work. Some days, nothing goes right, no matter how hard you try.
Narrator: I used to let one bad meeting ruin my entire day, even the parts that had nothing to do with work.
Narrator: [honestly] Last month, I made a real mistake in front of my whole team during a presentation. My mind went completely blank.
Narrator: For the rest of that day, I replayed the moment over and over, feeling embarrassed every single time.
Narrator: [thoughtful] That night, I talked to a close friend who also works in an office. She said something simple but useful.
Narrator: She said, a bad meeting is one hour of your day, not the whole day, and definitely not the whole month.

Narrator: [carefully] Since then, I've tried a small trick. When something goes wrong, I often give myself about ten quiet minutes to feel upset, though another person may need a different healthy pause.
Narrator: I let myself feel annoyed or embarrassed, fully, without pretending everything is fine when it clearly isn't.
Narrator: [reflective] After those ten minutes, I try to ask one question. What is one small thing I can control right now?
Narrator: Sometimes the answer is small, like sending one clear email, or simply taking a short walk outside the building.
Narrator: [practically] I also learned to separate one mistake from my whole ability as a worker. One error doesn't erase months of good work.
Narrator: I still have hard days, plenty of them. Nobody figures this out perfectly, no matter how experienced they become.
Narrator: [calmly] But now, a difficult morning doesn't automatically ruin my whole evening the way it used to.
Narrator: I go home, I eat dinner, and I remind myself that tomorrow is a completely new day at the office.

quiz.question: What did the narrator used to let one bad meeting do?
quiz.explanation: She used to let one bad meeting ruin her entire day, even unrelated parts.

quiz.question: What happened during her presentation last month?
options: She made a mistake in front of her whole team and her mind went blank
She was praised by her manager
She was not allowed to present
quiz.explanation: She made a real mistake during the presentation and her mind went completely blank.

quiz.question: What did her friend tell her about a bad meeting?
options: It's one hour of the day, not the whole day
quiz.explanation: Her friend said a bad meeting is one hour of the day, not the whole day or month.

quiz.question: What trick does the narrator now use after something goes wrong?
options: She gives herself ten minutes to feel upset, then asks what she can control
She takes the rest of the week off
quiz.explanation: She gives herself ten minutes to feel upset, then asks what small thing she can control.

quiz.question: What does the narrator remind herself about mistakes?
options: One error erases months of good work
One mistake doesn't erase her whole ability as a worker
quiz.explanation: She reminds herself that one mistake doesn't erase months of good work.

quiz.question: What did the friend separate?
options: One bad hour from the whole day
quiz.explanation: The event did not need to define everything.

quiz.question: What question follows the emotion?
options: What small thing can I control now?

quiz.question: Which small action is mentioned?
options: Send one clear email or walk briefly

quiz.question: What does one error not erase?
quiz.explanation: Ability is not reduced to one moment.
